summary: Prucalopride is a selective 5-HT4 receptor agonist (gastrointestinal prokinetic) indicated for chronic idiopathic constipation in adults. It stimulates colonic high-amplitude propagating contractions to increase bowel motility. Its label includes a warning for suicidal ideation and behavior and new-onset or worsening depression, generally within the first weeks of therapy. The usual dose is 2 mg once daily, reduced to 1 mg once daily in severe renal impairment.

dosage.d: Reassess benefit if no effect after 4 weeks

admin: Take once daily with or without food
May be taken at any consistent time of day
Reassess continued benefit if not effective after about 4 weeks
Monitor for new or worsening mood changes/suicidal thoughts
moa: Selective, high-affinity serotonin type-4 (5-HT4) receptor agonist; facilitates acetylcholine release in the enteric nervous system, enhancing colonic high-amplitude propagating contractions (HAPCs) and peristalsis, thereby increasing bowel motility. Devoid of clinically relevant activity at hERG/other 5-HT receptors at therapeutic doses.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to prucalopride (reactions: dyspnea, rash, pruritus, urticaria, facial edema)
Intestinal perforation or obstruction due to structural/functional gut wall disorder
Severe inflammatory intestinal conditions (Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, toxic megacolon/megarectum)
relative: History of depression or suicidal ideation
Severe/clinically unstable cardiovascular disease (use clinical judgment)
monitor: Mood and suicidal ideation (especially first weeks)

preg: Available human data are insufficient to identify drug-associated risks; animal studies showed no adverse developmental effects at high multiples of the human dose. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Excreted in breast milk (animal data show transfer); effects on the breastfed infant are unknown. Weigh developmental/health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need.
renal: Severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min): reduce to 1 mg once daily. No adjustment needed for mild-to-moderate impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment for mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment; use with caution in severe hepatic impairment (limited data).

moderate: Drugs that prolong gastrointestinal transit/anticholinergics - may reduce prokinetic effect
Other serotonergic agents - theoretical additive serotonergic effect (limited clinical significance)
minor: Ketoconazole (potent P-gp/CYP inhibitor) - small increase in prucalopride exposure, not clinically significant
Oral contraceptives - increased GI motility could theoretically affect absorption if vomiting/severe diarrhea occurs
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food

serious: Suicidal ideation and behavior / new-onset or worsening depression

monitoring: Mood, depression, and suicidal/self-injurious ideation (especially first few weeks)
Bowel movement frequency and symptom response
Continued need (reassess at ~4 weeks if ineffective)
counsel: Take once daily, with or without food
Headache, nausea, and diarrhea are most common and often improve after the first days
Stop the drug and contact your clinician immediately if you have unusual changes in mood, worsening depression, or thoughts of self-harm
It may take a few days to see benefit; tell your clinician if there is no improvement after 4 weeks
Report rash, swelling, or trouble breathing
Maintain adequate fluid and fiber intake
pk: First bowel movement often within ~2-3 h to first day
20-25 C; keep in original container, protect from moisture
pearls: Highly selective 5-HT4 agonist - designed to avoid the cardiac risks of older non-selective agents (cisapride/tegaserod)
Label warning for suicidal ideation/behavior and new-onset or worsening depression - counsel and monitor early
Reduce to 1 mg daily in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30)
Reassess benefit at ~4 weeks; discontinue if ineffective
missed: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time; do not take two doses to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Symptoms may include headache, nausea, and diarrhea (exaggerated pharmacologic effects). Management is supportive with attention to fluid/electrolyte balance from diarrhea; no specific antidote.
